text:
kevin: seeing a steady regression in request completion after we enabled token hot-reload. starts as a small tail-latency bump, then ~30s later a bunch of requests hang.
amira: do you have the client config? pool size / keepalive / whether you use httpx limits?
kevin: default AsyncRedwoodClient, no pool overrides. running 100 concurrent coros. repro attached below:
```
# repro
python examples/hot_reload_stall.py --concurrency 100 --rotate-every 6
```
kevin: log snippets:
```
WARNING httpcore._backends.auto: Reusing closed transport (fd=77)
ERROR httpx._exceptions.ReadError: Connection was closed unexpectedly
DEBUG connpool: returned connection id=77 to pool (state=usable)
```
oscar: that debug line is concerning. if a connection fails mid-request we should mark it dead, not put it back as usable.
amira: agreed. also noticed AsyncRedwoodClient.__aenter__ annotation returns Any in our stub which hides bad lifecycle usage (global client objects that never get closed). I'll open a dtype PR.
kevin: workaround: calling `await client.aclose()` right after token refresh clears the backlog but is disruptive. maybe we can drain just-bad connections?
oscar: proposal: add `pool.evict_on_error=True` and `pool.min_idle=0` defaults during auth-path; implement a fast path to mark transport closed on read/write errors or 4xx auth responses.
jade: small DX ask: can we add a typed helper `async with AsyncRedwoodClient.for_short_lived()` that sets aggressive pool limits for ephemeral workloads? would help sample apps.
ci-bot: queued test: devex/conn-evict-ci #204.
amira: plan: 1) patch pool to not re-enqueue trashed transports and increment metric `connpool.evictions.error`; 2) tighten typing for async context manager to prevent misuse; 3) add docs blurb about token rotation patterns + sample snippet using aclose or short-lived clients.
oscar: I'll PR the pool change and a unit test that simulates ConnectionResetError during request and verifies eviction.
kevin: thanks, will test the patch. shared gist with repro: https://gist.github.com/kevin/hotreload-stall. updating issue #2601 with logs. :thumbsup:
